catalog_quote: 7. Tone. Akɔ:sé has a two tone terraced level system. It can be analysed as consisting basically of high and low tones, and the following features: 1) automatic downdrift 2) downstep 3) upstep There are three tone glides analysed as combinations of two separate level tones: ^ or HL, ˇ or LH, ... (cf. section 5.7). The first two are the most common glides. Under elision features are grouped: loss of low tones, tone glide reduction and low tone replacement (see chapter 2). ... [p. 18] The major P-word has an obligatory nucleus, which is optionally preceded by a premargin of one (or two) syllable(s) and/or optionally followed by a postmargin of one or two syllables. The nucleus is characterized by the least restriction in the occurrence of phonemes, by the presence of certain allophones and the occurrence of the features of labialization and palatalization. sources.citation: Ekanjume, Beatrice. 2008. The phonological phrase as a prosodic domain in Akóóse. Journal of West African Languages 35(1-2): 57ff. (open access, JWAL site)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: p. 60: 'we find the nouns featuring with the following tones: a high tone, a low tone, a low-high tone, a high and low tone, a low and low tone, and a low and high tone in the root ... The initial vowel of one of the adjectives (like most initial vowels in Akóóse) is toneless ... it gets its tone from default Low at the postlexical level.' Rules found (p. 66): high tone spreading, vowel deletion, vowel shortening, vowel insertion, tone docking, default Low. No mention of stress or accent as a property of Akoose anywhere in the article (the only 'stress' strings are in titles of cited works).
sources.locator: printed p. 60 (PDF p. 4), section 1 data discussion; conclusions p. 66-67
sources.note: Only open-access modern prosody paper on Akoose; downloaded now; describes root tone patterns (H, L, LH, HL..), toneless prefixes with default L, HTS and tone docking; no stress/accent -- corroborates the tonal coding.

sources.citation: Hedinger, Robert. 1985 (rev. 1987, 1988, 2000). Some issues in the establishment of an orthography for Akɔɔse. SIL Cameroon ms., 8 pp. (SIL archive, via the Internet Archive)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: Treats Akoose as tonal with High, Low, Rising, Falling and Downstepped High to be marked orthographically; discusses which tone to leave unmarked by text frequency. No stress or accent mentioned.
